title: Summer Beach Picnic Board
seo_title: Beach Picnic Charcuterie Board for 6–10: What to Pack
description: A beach picnic charcuterie board for 6–10: Parmesan, sharp cheddar, pepperoni, hard salami, mango, dried pineapple, macadamia nuts, Triscuits and pita chips.
hook: Portable and heat-tolerant: a beach board built from foods that travel well, with tropical fruit for the mood.
why: A beach board has to handle heat and sand, so it uses foods that hold up: hard, aged Parmesan and sharp cheddar, and dry-cured pepperoni and salami instead of soft cheese and delicate prosciutto. Sturdy Triscuits and pita chips don't go soft in the humidity.

Mango, dried pineapple and macadamia nuts give it a tropical feel, and salsa with pita chips makes a natural gathering spot. Keep it in a cooler until you serve, and eat it within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F.

timeline.what: Pack everything in a cooler with ice packs.
Slice the cheese at home and seal it in containers.
Set up the board at the beach, in the shade.
Add the fruit and crackers last.

faq.q: What's a good charcuterie board for the beach?
faq.a: Hard cheeses like Parmesan and aged cheddar, dry salami and pepperoni, mango, dried fruit, nuts, salsa and sturdy crackers or chips.

faq.q: How do you keep a beach board safe in the heat?
faq.a: Keep everything in a cooler with ice packs, set up in the shade and serve it within 1 hour when it's above 90°F.

faq.q: How do you keep sand off?
faq.a: Build it on a board with a lid or in a shallow container, and only open it when you're ready to eat.
